itens.t: SpaceX achieves historic first tower catch of Starship upper stage in Flight 15
itens.r: SpaceX reached a major milestone in its megarocket development during the 15th test flight of Starship on Friday. The mission featured the first-ever successful tower catch of the Starship upper stage, marking a monumental leap toward full reusability. While the upper stage was secured by the launch tower arms, the Super Heavy booster encountered issues and diverted into the Gulf of Mexico. Engineers are now analyzing telemetry data to refine future flights and optimize booster recovery operations. This breakthrough brings commercial deep-space transport closer to everyday reality.
itens.d:
SpaceX achieved a historic milestone during the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket when its tower arms successfully caught the Ship upper stage in Texas. The upper stage completed its return trip 22.5 hours after lifting off, nestling into the chopstick arms in an unprecedented maneuver.

While the Ship recovery was a major success, the Super Heavy booster did not achieve the same fate. It experienced a low-fuel alarm and diverted to a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico instead of being caught by the launch pad tower.
itens.e:
SpaceX achieved a historic milestone during the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket when its launch pad tower arms successfully caught the Ship upper stage in Texas. The upper stage completed its return trip 22.5 hours after lifting off, nestling into the chopstick arms in an unprecedented maneuver. While this recovery was a major success, the Super Heavy booster did not achieve the same fate.

This outcome matters greatly for the future of rapid rocket reusability, as the booster experienced a low-fuel alarm and was forced to divert to a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico instead of being caught by the tower. This suggests that while upper-stage recovery techniques are advancing rapidly, perfecting booster catch operations under varying flight conditions remains a complex engineering hurdle for the aerospace program.

One risk is that similar fuel management anomalies could delay future flight schedules. Observers should watch how engineers address the low-fuel alarm issue on the Super Heavy booster ahead of subsequent test flights to determine if structural adjustments to the recovery profile will be necessary.

The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index lost 190.03 points to close at 5,100.5, extending its losses into a third consecutive session. Meanwhile, the Korean won strengthened against the US dollar during the trading day.
itens.e:
South Korean stocks dropped sharply by more than 3 percent on Monday as foreign investors sold technology shares, extending the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index losses into a third consecutive session to close at 5,100.5 points. The broad decline was driven by lingering concerns over the artificial intelligence boom following fallout at Nvidia, even as the Korean won strengthened against the US dollar during the trading day.

This sudden market correction matters directly to institutional and retail investors holding technology-heavy portfolios, highlighting how quickly sentiment can shift due to overseas sector volatility. One risk is that persistent jitters surrounding artificial intelligence valuations could trigger further sell-offs. Market participants will watch to see if foreign investors continue liquidating tech shares or if stabilization in overseas markets can restore confidence in the upcoming sessions.

itens.t: Webb telescope reveals intricate star formation and jets in NGC 7129
itens.r: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope captured stunning details of active star birth within the cosmic cloud NGC 7129. The imagery highlights powerful stellar jets interacting with surrounding gas and dust.
itens.d:
NASA utilized the James Webb Space Telescope to capture a detailed infrared image of the star-forming region NGC 7129. The observation reveals how gravity pulls together gas to form stars, while young stars emit powerful jets and winds that shape the surrounding gas.

The captured imagery shows younger stars located on the right in red regions and more mature stars on the left in gold-colored gas. Opaque dust also forms in these cool stellar atmospheres and can obstruct visible-light images.

itens.t: Escaping gases tear apart brightening comet, releasing massive dust clouds
itens.r: Intense solar heat caused ice beneath a comet's surface to vaporize rapidly, fracturing the body and spewing enormous amounts of dust into space. The volatile outburst dramatically increased the celestial object's brightness.
itens.d:
Comet 220P/McNaught experienced a dramatic outburst as the sun's heat turned subsurface ice into gas, spewing massive dust clouds into space and brightening significantly. The periodic comet was originally discovered in 2004 and orbits the sun every five and a half years.

On June 14, as it approached its closest point to the sun, the comet unexpectedly burst into life and brightened by thousands of times. This rare event brought the celestial object within range for observation by small amateur telescopes and binoculars.
